citation: 8 U.S.C. § 1324a; discussed in Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387, 403-407 (2012)
raw_text: The Immigration Reform and Control Act imposes civil fines and, for repeated violations, criminal penalties on employers who knowingly hire unauthorized workers. Congress considered and rejected imposing federal criminal penalties on an unauthorized alien for the act of merely seeking or engaging in unauthorized employment; that conduct carries no federal criminal sanction.

citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 13-2928(C) (S.B. 1070 § 5(C)); held preempted in Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387 (2012)
raw_text: It is a class 1 misdemeanor for an unauthorized alien to knowingly apply for work, solicit work in a public place, or perform work as an employee or independent contractor in this state.

Every alien eighteen years of age and over shall at all times carry with them any certificate of alien registration issued to them. Willful failure to do so is a federal misdemeanor. This registration scheme is comprehensive and occupies the field of alien registration.

citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 13-1509 (S.B. 1070 § 3); held preempted in Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387 (2012)
raw_text: It is a class 1 misdemeanor for a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to willfully fail to complete or carry an alien registration document, if the federal registration requirements apply to that person.

citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. §§ 23-211 to 23-212 (Legal Arizona Workers Act); upheld in Chamber of Commerce v. Whiting, 563 U.S. 582 (2011)
raw_text: Every employer in this state shall verify the employment eligibility of a newly hired employee through the federal E-Verify program. An employer who knowingly employs an unauthorized alien is subject to suspension or revocation of its business license.

citation: 8 U.S.C. § 1357(a)(2); discussed in Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387, 408-410 (2012)
raw_text: A federal immigration officer may arrest an alien without a warrant only where the officer has reason to believe the alien is in the United States in violation of the immigration laws and is likely to escape before a warrant can be obtained. This warrantless-arrest authority for suspected civil removability is conferred on federal immigration officers only; it is not extended to state or local law enforcement officers.

citation: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 13-3883(A)(5) (S.B. 1070 § 6); held preempted in Arizona v. United States, 567 U.S. 387, 408-410 (2012)
raw_text: A state or local peace officer, without a warrant, may arrest a person if the officer has probable cause to believe that the person has committed a public offense that makes the person removable from the United States.
